idea.description: SASRec predicts the next item by applying causal self-attention to interaction histories. Learned item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks with residual connections, normalization and dropout. Final sequence features score candidates through shared item embeddings. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781)
idea.motivation: Attention selects relevant past interactions, combining recent-action signals with longer dependencies. This addresses varying interaction density; it does not directly solve unseen-item or zero-history cold start.
idea.implementation_notes: The paper uses shifted next-item supervision, sampled binary cross-entropy and Adam. For this task, retain sasrec_perdataset routing across Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the 200-epoch environment default. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts under the trial directory. Select using the pinned macro validation HR@10 only. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), measured metrics with definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Update the predictor writer whenever architecture changes. No experiments or benchmark gains are reported here.
idea.pseudocode:
for each category:
    load unchanged training split
    build padded histories and shifted positive targets
    sample unseen negative items
    features = causal_SASRec(item_embeddings + position_embeddings)
    loss = masked_BCE(features · positive_embeddings, 1)
         + masked_BCE(features · negative_embeddings, 0)
    optimize; save model and matching predictor configuration
select trials using the common four-category macro validation HR@10

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential attention-based sequential recommender.
originality.negative: The supplied idea repeats the existing SASRec baseline without a concrete new mechanism.

future_potential.positive: Permitted titles and descriptions could support a future content-aware extension for rare items.
future_potential.negative: That extension is a hypothesis; its value requires validation within the shared budget.

code_difficulty.positive: Starting from the supplied SASRec baseline limits implementation work.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal masking, padding, dataset routing and training–prediction consistency require care.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
